institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was important that the destination had a strong focus on nature. I also thought a lot about the language, as I wanted to be able to communicate with the locals without them having to switch to another language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I felt there were many different documents to keep track of all the time, but this is not only the case for Tromsø.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person, but he was responsible for all international students, which made it challenging for him to provide detailed assistance. This often resulted in very brief replies, and at times, it felt like he hadn't fully read the email before responding.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and accessible. Tromsø has a student housing portal called Samskipnaden. Here, you can search for and secure student accommodation in various locations across Tromsø at different price ranges. They prioritize international students, and I haven't heard of anyone who applied and didn't get housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is important to check the time it takes to get from your housing to the campus, not just the distance! Tromsø is not as flat as Denmark.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember this part so good, but i just followed the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was able to fing alot of information on the UiT website, they had an email and when we arrived we could just drop in fore a personal meating

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I wanted, and the ones I didn't get were due to my sending institution. When exploring the classes, it's important to note that if you follow the link for international students, you won't be able to see the classes taught in Norwegian.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic about all the emails you receive from UiT. They send reminder emails to everyone, regardless of whether you've already submitted the requested document or not. That's why it's a good idea to keep track of what you've sent, so you don't get too confused when they follow up on something you've already handled.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty level of my courses varied greatly. I had one course where the main focus was reading scientific articles and presenting them, which was at a lower academic level compared to the University of Copenhagen. Then I had a pharmacology course where the teaching was on par with KU, but the exam was easier. Lastly, I took an immunology course, where the difficulty level was very similar to KU throughout the entire course. All of them 10 ECTS

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to what I'm used to at CPHU. We had lectures and practical sessions that were closely aligned with the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recogment to look at DNT youth. They organize trips to various cabins with other young people at really affordable prices.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips and explore Northern Norway. Places like Senja, Lyngen, Lofoten, Harstad, and Alta are highly recommended. Additionally, it's possible to rent cross-country skis when the snow falls, which is also a must-try experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Norway was very similar to Denmark, so cute easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live in student housing and talk to the locals in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the love to the nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Bring all the outdoor gear you have at home.
- Don't be embarrassed to try speaking Norwegian, even if it feels a bit outside your comfort zone.  
- If you enjoy a particular sport, join a local team or club—it's a great way to connect with the locals!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're even slightly considering staying for two semesters instead of one, apply for it right away. It seems possible to withdraw the application later, but you cannot request an extension once you're already there. I knew several people who wanted to stay longer but couldn't because they hadn't applied in advance. This is a rule from KU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new people I've met and the amazing nature experiences I've had.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I am not sure
